title: massachusetts top court reprimands judge ice arrest evasion case 2026 09 10
text:
BOSTON, Sept 10 (Reuters) - Massachusetts' highest court on Thursday publicly reprimanded a judge who was criminally charged during the first Trump administration with helping a migrant avoid arrest by a federal immigration agent at her courthouse.
The discipline imposed by the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial ​Court marked the final chapter in a years-long legal saga involving Judge Shelley Joseph, who agreed to face a ‌disciplinary probe in exchange for U.S. prosecutors dropping their case against her in 2022 after the end of President Donald Trump's first term.
The criminal case was filed in 2019 and became a high-profile example of clashes between the Trump administration and local officials who have resisted federal immigration crackdowns in both of his terms.
Prosecutors ​alleged that Joseph, in April 2018, allowed a Dominican man being arraigned in a criminal case before her to avoid ​being detained by an agent with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement by letting him leave the building ⁠through a rear door in her Newton, Massachusetts courthouse.
After the criminal case against the judge was dropped, the Massachusetts Judicial Conduct Commission ​launched disciplinary proceedings in 2024, seeking to have Joseph suspended and referred to the state legislature and governor for removal.
But at the state's ​supreme court, the commission only requested a public reprimand after a judicial disciplinary hearing officer in November concluded it failed to prove Joseph knew about the plan to help the defendant evade ICE.
The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court in its 6-0 unsigned opinion
, opens new tab
 on Thursday adopted the recommendation to publicly reprimand the judge.
The court ​said such discipline was warranted as Joseph had violated the judicial code of conduct by holding an off-the-record discussion of the defendant's ​case with his lawyer and suggesting, after learning about the ICE officer's presence, that she could have the man jailed overnight.
The high court said Joseph's ‌comments created ⁠a perception that she was willing to keep the man detained "without a legal basis to do so to help him avoid Federal custody – a purpose not authorized by the bail statute."
A lawyer for Joseph did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Her attorneys had argued that the court should dismiss the disciplinary case entirely, saying the only reason it was brought was because of a false allegation ​that had led to her wrongful ​prosecution.
The court in Thursday's opinion ⁠acknowledged Joseph's conduct was "less severe" than that of other judges it had previously publicly reprimanded or censured.
"However, given the public nature of the proceedings against the respondent, and to ensure that there is ​no misunderstanding as to what she is – and is not – being reprimanded for, we conclude that the ​respondent should be ⁠publicly reprimanded," the court wrote.
The case is In Re: Shelley M. Joseph, Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court, No. OE-0157.
For the Massachusetts Judicial Conduct Commission: Judith Fabricant
For Joseph: Elizabeth Mulvey of Libby Hoopes Brooks & Mulvey
